Company Report
Microsoft Corporation (MSFT)
A Closer Look at the Quarter
Total revenue of $81.3B (+17% Y/Y reported and 15% on a CC basis) was nicely above our $80.2B
forecast and the Street's similar $80.3B estimate (+15% Y/Y). Further, and more importantly, Azure
revenue growth of 38% Y/Y CC, which exceeded mgmt's guidance that had called for 37% growth
Y/Y, although this did fall just shy of buy-side expectations. For more specifics on the Azure
performance this quarter, please see below.
On a segment basis, Productivity and Business Processes (PBP) revenue of ~$34.1B (+14% Y/
Y CC) was above our $33.46B projection. Meanwhile, Intelligent Cloud revenue of $32.9B (+28%
Y/Y CC vs. 27% growth reported previously) also exceeded our $32.45B estimate this quarter.
Finally, More Personal Computing (MPC) revenue of nearly $14.3B (-3% Y/Y CC) edged our $14.26B
forecast.
On the heels of a very strong first quarter, F2Q Commercial bookings astoundingly grew 228%
Y/Y CC, which reflects significant further acceleration from the already massive 111% growth
rate reported previously and ~30% Y/Y growth reported in F4Q. The strength this quarter was
predominantly driven by Azure commitments from OpenAI, as well as Anthropic, and with healthy
growth across its core annuity sales motions. More specifically, this includes the incremental
$250B in Azure commitments from the recent OpenAI agreement.
Despite continued high capex, reported gross margins were very good at 68.0%, easily above our
67.0% target and the Street's ~67.1% forecast. Further, OMs of 47.1% were much better than
expected and easily surpassed our and the Street's 45.3% target. In addition, under the equity
method of accounting, OpenAI contributed a $9.978B gain (vs. a $4.061B loss previously) to Other
Income & Expense (OI&E), and a $7.583B net gain (vs. $3.086B net loss previously). Non-GAAP
EPS - excluding this component - was $4.14 vs. our $3.96 estimate and the Street's $3.91 forecast.

Microsoft reported another solid result for F2Q, but it ultimately fell short of more 
lofty market expectations, in particular for Azure growth. While most investors 
continue to hone in on this as the most important KPI, mgmt. again made it clear 
Azure is bearing the brunt of current supply constraints as they prioritize GPU 
allocation in support of AI usage in first-party apps and R&D to accelerate product 
innovation in pursuit of higher margin, recurring software opportunities up the 
stack. So while Azure growth still came in 1pt above guidance at +38% y/y @CC, 
this was shy of what we believe was a buyside bogey of >39%+ and what mgmt. 
indicated would have been >40% had they allocated all incremental GPU capacity 
in F1H26 to Azure. Importantly, we'd highlight Azure is still growing well above the 
market, guided to sustain 37-38% growth in F3Q and we believe can likely persist 
near here for several more quarters off a higher base.
From a margin and LTV perspective we believe the application layer has and is still 
generally perceived as highly strategic ground on which Microsoft has incumbent 
advantages. But we'd argue it is also the last area to see tangible benefits as AI 
monetization works its way up the stack, and is more than ever viewed as at risk of 
disruption and/or devaluation, which is weighing on sentiment. That story has yet 
to play out in our view, so while foregoing Azure revenue now for high-margin 
application and consumer SW opportunity ahead seems a sensible long-term 
strategy, it puts the onus on Microsoft to deliver before it will get credit. We continue 
to see more evidence of steadily growing traction, including new disclosure this 
quarter of 15m paid M365 Copilot seats (accelerating q/q and +160% y/y), paid 
GitHub Copilot subs now up to 4.7m (+75% y/y) and >100k medical providers using
